subject: Northbridge: request for customer-visible model/version changelogs + deprecation policy + notifications
body:
From: Avery Chen <avery.chen@northbridgecm.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Priya Nair <priya.nair@northbridgecm.com>
Date: Fri, Oct 3, 2025 at 9:14 AM
Subject: Northbridge: request for customer-visible model/version changelogs + deprecation policy + notifications

Hi Marissa,

Following up from yesterday’s security review track.

For us to proceed with Redwood Private (VPC), we need clarity on change visibility for models served in our environment:

1) Customer-visible model/version release notes / changelog
- When a model version is promoted (or the underlying runtime/quant profile changes), do we get a changelog that explains what changed and why?
- We need an audit trail we can show to our change-management board.

2) Deprecation policy
- How do you define and communicate deprecations (e.g., tokenizer changes, model alias re-pointing, quantization profile retirement)?
- What are typical timelines?

3) Notifications
- Do you support email/webhook notifications for model changes? If not today, what is the planned approach?

Our blockers are mainly around “silent” updates and the ability to map a behavior change to a specific version/rollout.

Thanks,
Avery

—
Avery Chen
Director, Platform Security
Northbridge Capital Markets



From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Avery Chen <avery.chen@northbridgecm.com>
Cc: Priya Nair <priya.nair@northbridgecm.com>
Date: Fri, Oct 3, 2025 at 10:02 AM
Subject: Re: Northbridge: request for customer-visible model/version changelogs + deprecation policy + notifications

Hi Avery,

This is helpful context — thank you.

On (1) and (2), we do have the building blocks today (version pinning, promotions tracked internally), but the customer-facing “single place” changelog/release-notes experience is something we’re actively standardizing across Hosted/Dedicated/Private. I’m pulling in our release/process owner and the Console backend lead to give you a precise answer on:
- what you can expect immediately for Private (including evidence/audit trail)
- what’s coming in the next couple of months (customer-visible notes + notifications)

I’ll come back with a concrete proposal + sample output.

Best,
Marissa

—
Marissa Cole
Director of Product, Console & Rollouts
Redwood Inference

Can you help me respond today with specifics?

Northbridge is evaluating Private (VPC) and needs:
- customer-visible release notes/changelog for model version promotions + metadata changes
- clear deprecation semantics/timelines (especially alias repoints, tokenizer/runtime req changes, quant profile retirement)
- notification expectations (email/webhook) — even if “not yet”, need roadmap language

Ask: please send me
1) what we can provide immediately (even if internal export) for Private customers
2) what the standardized v1 story is (schema + changelog generator) and how we avoid leaking internal-only details
3) any constraints/wording we should use (e.g., “quality improvements” must be qualified)

Ideally include a short bullet answer I can paste + a one-paragraph “policy” section.

From: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwoodinference.com>

Date: Fri, Oct 3, 2025 at 11:04 AM
Subject: Re: Fwd: Northbridge asks for customer-visible model/version changelogs + deprecation policy + notifications

Here’s language you can use (feel free to edit tone).

What we can provide immediately:
- For any model/version promotion in a customer environment, we can export a versioned “change record” with timestamp, actor (service/system), environment, and the before/after version identifiers. For Private, this can ship as part of the upgrade bundle artifacts.
- We can also provide a rollback note: the previously-active version identifier and the procedure for pinning/rollback.

What is being standardized (v1):
- We’re rolling out a single metadata schema per served model/variant/quant profile (semantic versions + compatibility constraints + runtime/tokenizer requirements + deprecation flags).
- From these structured fields and promotion/change events, we generate customer-visible release notes with consistent categories (breaking, security, perf, quality, bugfix, deprecation) and a separate internal-only audit record.
- Public vs internal: notes will be generated from “public” fields; internal fields (incident refs, vendor/kernel details, account-specific info) are never rendered externally.

Notifications:
- Today: internal webhook plumbing exists, but we don’t have GA customer self-serve subscriptions (email/webhook) across all deployments.
- Near-term: we plan to expose programmatic access (API/Console) to the release notes feed and per-model history; notifications will come after the feed is stable.

Deprecation policy (suggested phrasing):
- We will mark a deprecation in metadata and include it in the customer-visible notes with a timeline. Deprecations do not change behavior by themselves; they indicate intent to retire a version/alias/profile.
- Breaking changes (incl. tokenizer incompatibilities, required runtime changes, or alias repoints that materially change behavior) are published as breaking, include rollout/rollback guidance, and respect pinned versions.

One nuance: avoid guaranteeing metric deltas. We can say “performance improvements in common workloads” or “quality improvements based on internal evals” and link to methodology (or keep it high-level).

If you want, I can mock an example “release note” entry you can share.

—
Connor O’Brien
Release Engineering
Redwood Inference



From: Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwoodinference.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, Oct 3, 2025 at 12:37 PM
Subject: Re: Fwd: Northbridge asks for customer-visible model/version changelogs + deprecation policy + notifications

+1 to Connor’s draft. Adding a bit more detail on what Private customers will actually see.

For Private:
- The upgrade bundle can include a machine-readable release-notes artifact (JSON) + a human-readable summary (Markdown/PDF) that lists:
  - model identifier + semantic version
  - deployment availability (Hosted/Dedicated/Private) and bundle applicability
  - compatibility constraints (tokenizer/runtime requirements)
  - change categories + severity
  - deprecations + effective dates
  - rollback/pinning guidance
- Internally we also emit audit events for create/update/promote/deprecate. We can provide evidence (export) to Northbridge’s compliance team, but we should be explicit that the customer-visible notes are curated/redacted.

On notifications:
- In the interim, we can commit to “no silent changes” for their pinned versions (i.e., if they pin, we won’t move them without an explicit promotion they control).
- If they use an alias (“latest”), they should expect it to move as part of a rollout; the release notes feed is the mechanism to understand what moved.

If you want a clean deprecation timeline statement: we usually give at least 90 days for planned deprecations in enterprise contexts, but we should caveat security issues may accelerate.

Chloe

—
Chloe Martin
Engineering Manager, Console Backend
Redwood Inference



From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>

Subject: Re: Northbridge: request for customer-visible model/version changelogs + deprecation policy + notifications

Hi Avery,

Thanks again — below is the concrete view of how we handle this for Private (VPC) and what’s coming next.

1) Customer-visible model/version release notes (change visibility)
- For model version promotions and metadata changes, we can provide a versioned change record that includes: timestamps, environment, what moved (before/after version identifiers), and a human-readable summary of the change category (breaking/security/perf/quality/bugfix/deprecation) plus rollback/pinning guidance.
- For Private specifically, we can ship this alongside the upgrade bundle artifacts (machine-readable JSON + a human-readable summary) so your CAB has a durable record.
- Separately, we maintain an internal audit trail (who/what/when/where) for compliance and support; customer-visible notes are generated from curated “public” fields and exclude internal-only details.

2) Deprecation policy
- Deprecations are explicitly marked and included in the release notes with a timeline and guidance. A deprecation flag is an announcement of intent; it does not itself change your currently pinned behavior.
- Breaking changes (e.g., tokenizer incompatibilities, runtime requirement changes, alias repoints that materially change behavior) are called out as breaking with rollback guidance. Pinned versions remain stable until you choose to adopt a newer version.
- For enterprise customers, we generally target >=90 days notice for planned deprecations; exceptions may apply for urgent security fixes.

3) Notifications
- Today, we don’t yet have GA self-serve customer subscriptions (email/webhook) for model change notifications across all deployments.
- Near-term, we’re standardizing a single release-notes feed / per-model history (Console + API) that you can poll and integrate into your own change-management workflows. Notification subscriptions are planned after the feed is stable.

If it’s helpful, we can share a sample “release note” entry format and align on the fields your CAB expects to see (e.g., severity, compatibility constraints, effective dates).

Would you like to review this in the next working session with Priya (15–20 min)?

Best,
Marissa

—
Marissa Cole
Director of Product, Console & Rollouts
Redwood Inference
